newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- State transport company Transnet has agreed to take over 2.1 million rand in outstanding rates owed by its employees to three Western Cape municipalities.
- The government must find an extra 230 million rand to pay a once-off increase to about 170,000 public sector workers eligible for the payment.
- Lower food prices helped offset rising import costs in February, containing producer inflation at 9.3 percent from January's 9.2 percent, according to the Central Statistical Service.

- Chemicals manufacturer Sentrachem posted a 217 million rand attributable loss for the six months to February, as one-off losses from ill-judged forward exchange contracts at subsidiary Sanachem took effect.

- The merger between Perskor and black group Kagiso Publishing is to go ahead after Perskor minority shareholders backed a new structure designed to break the impasse which blocked the deal eight months ago.
- Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, facing the greatest threat to his power in more than three decades of rule, failed to respond to a rebel ultimatum for him to negotiate his resignation.

- The Agricultural Research Council is pulling out all the stops to save the South African honey production and pollination service industries following extensive damage caused by the northward migration of the Cape bee, which is unproductive outside its natural domain.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Anglovaal, the major shareholder of the troubled Crusader Life insurance company, confirmed it will contribute 20 million rand to a buyout of Crusader by the Hollard Insurance Group.
- Japanese tyre company Bridgestone could invest more than 44 million rand to improve quality and productivity at its South African tyre plants, according to Bridgestone head Yoichiro Kaizaki.

- The advisers to soon-to-be-privatised Sun Air have received more than 10 bids for the airline. Among them is one from Richard Branson's Virgin Atlantic, which bid with Bhekilanga, a consortium of six black empowerment groupings.

- Sharp divisions have emerged within South Africa's largest trade union federation, Cosatu, over privatisation policies and a planned nationwide May 12 strike against the government's Employment Standards Bill, union officials and sources said.
SAKE-BEELD
- Mercedes-Benz South Africa has become the latest motor vehicle company to form its own financing firm. Mercedes-Benz Finance will be a subsidiary of Daimler-Benz Interservices

- A new draft policy document has proposed the demise of the state tender board and the nine provincial tender boards and their replacement by an office to oversee the departmental and provincial officials who would handle their own tenders.
- The rand fell early on Thursday to its lowest level against the dollar in five weeks, but recovered slightly after Reserve Bank intervention.
- Inflation in the prices of imported goods was the largest single factor which pushed up February's producer price inflation, which went up by 0.4 percent for the month of February.
MAIL & GUARDIAN
- British firm Biwater is at the centre of a growing row over the privatisation of the water supply in Nelspruit in Mpumalanga province.
- A pilot programme to spearhead land reform has fallen flat, with most provinces spending only a fraction of the budgets set aside for the purpose.
- The South African Law Commission has proposed draft legislation to allow "passive euthanasia" -- withholding life support or life-saving treatment.
